title: Improve Vehicle Controls: Keyboard Handling, Stability Assistance & Gamepad Support
description:
## What
Comprehensive overhaul of vehicle control and input handling across desktop and console form factors. This epic addresses the extreme sensitivity and sudden spinouts experienced during keyboard driving by introducing digital input smoothing, speed-sensitive steering scaling, Traction Control (TCS), Electronic Stability Control (ESC), and dynamic drift recovery assist. Furthermore, it adds native cross-platform gamepad support with analog steering, progressive trigger acceleration/braking, configurable deadzones, and seamless input switching.

## Why
Currently, driving with digital keyboard keys is frustratingly twitchy. Because keys provide instantaneous 0 or 1 input, a brief tap snaps the steering wheels to full lock in under 0.15 seconds, and full engine torque instantly overpowers the rear wheels in turns, causing uncontrollable drifts and snap spinouts even on slight turns. In addition, standard WASD controls and gamepad controllers are not supported, severely limiting accessibility and game feel.

## Reasoning
Arcade racing games (e.g. GeneRally, TrackMania, Micro Machines, modern simcade titles) bridge the gap between digital inputs and physical tire models using:
1. Input smoothing & speed-sensitive steering limits (attenuating steering lock at speed).
2. Stability and traction assists (preventing wheelspin on throttle and catching snap oversteer).
3. First-class gamepad controller integration for analog precision.

## How this serves the project
Transforms TDRace from an unforgiving, spin-prone simulation into a responsive, accessible, and thrilling arcade racing experience whether played with keyboard, gamepad, or touch.

## Assumptions
- Keyboard controls will default to intuitive WASD + Arrow keys with arcade assists enabled by default.
- Assists can be tuned or toggled off for pro/simulation players.
- Gamepad support will work across desktop platforms (Linux, macOS, Windows) and Web/WASM seamlessly.
close_reason: done

title: Implement digital input smoothing, progressive steering ramps, and speed-sensitive scaling
description:
## What
Implement digital input filtering and smoothing for keyboard controls, including configurable rise/return rates, progressive steering curves, non-linear center response, speed-sensitive steering angle attenuation, and standard WASD + Arrow keybindings.

## Why
Keyboard inputs are binary. Currently, pressing a turn key snaps steering to maximum lock in ~0.13 seconds. At high speeds, this instant steering deflection creates massive lateral forces that immediately induce uncontrolled spinouts. Standard WASD bindings are also missing.

## Reasoning
Implementing a digital input filter that ramps steering angle smoothly based on delta time, combined with an exponential center curve and inverse speed attenuation, allows micro-corrections and high-speed stability while retaining sharp responsiveness for tight hairpin turns.

## Considerations
- Must maintain deterministic physics and replay compatibility.
- Rise speed should be fast enough to feel responsive, while return-to-center must be snappy to avoid sluggishness.
- Support dual layouts: WASD (W=gas, S=brake/rev, A=left, D=right) and Arrow Keys simultaneously.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Digital steering ramps up smoothly with configurable rise and return rates.
- [ ] Maximum steering lock scales inversely with vehicle speed to prevent sudden high-speed snap spins.
- [ ] WASD and Arrow Keys both work out-of-the-box for driving and menu navigation.
- [ ] Non-linear steering response allows subtle straight-line corrections without twitchiness.
close_reason: Implemented digital input smoothing, progressive steering ramps, speed-sensitive scaling, and WASD/Arrow key support

title: Implement Electronic Stability Control (ESC), Traction Control (TCS), and Drift Recovery Assist
description:
## What
Implement arcade driver assistance systems in the core vehicle physics engine:
1. Traction Control System (TCS): modulates drive torque when rear wheel slip exceeds grip limits.
2. Electronic Stability Control (ESC): dampens high yaw velocity rates and counteracts unintended spinouts.
3. Counter-Steer / Drift Recovery Assist: applies subtle self-aligning torque when recovering from slides.

## Why
With RWD physics and realistic Pacejka friction ellipses, full throttle during cornering consumes 100% of available tire grip for longitudinal drive, causing instant loss of lateral grip and immediate spinout. Digital keys cannot feather the throttle or rapidly counter-steer like a human driver with a steering wheel.

## Reasoning
Simulating active vehicle stability control bridges the gap between realistic tire physics and fun arcade playability. TCS prevents power-oversteer on corner exits, while ESC prevents the rear end from overtaking the front during gentle turns.

## Considerations
- Must not prevent intentional power slides when the driver holds handbrake or counter-steers intentionally.
- Assists should have configurable strength presets (High, Medium, Off/Pro).
- All calculations must be deterministic for physics substepping.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] TCS prevents instant wheelspin and snap oversteer when accelerating out of corners.
- [ ] ESC stabilizes vehicle yaw during sudden transitions and prevents unrecoverable spins on small turns.
- [ ] Drivers can still initiate and hold power drifts when applying handbrake or intentional steering lock.
- [ ] Assist strength can be configured or disabled.
close_reason: done

title: Add native cross-platform gamepad support (analog sticks, triggers, and button mappings)
description:
## What
Integrate native cross-platform gamepad support into `tdrace-app` with analog steering sticks, analog throttle/brake triggers, D-Pad, face buttons, deadzone calibration, and hot-plugging.

## Why
The user specifically requested gamepad support. Analog sticks and triggers provide continuous proportional control over steering, acceleration, and braking, which is the gold standard for top-down arcade racing games.

## Reasoning
Using a lightweight, cross-platform gamepad abstraction (compatible with Macroquad/desktop/web) allows seamless plug-and-play support for Xbox, PlayStation, Nintendo Switch, and generic USB/Bluetooth controllers.

## Considerations
- Analog stick deadzones (e.g. 10-15%) to prevent stick drift.
- Non-linear stick sensitivity curve for precise center control.
- Simultaneous input support: seamlessly transition between Gamepad, Keyboard, and Touch without restarts.
- Gamepad menu navigation (D-pad/stick for selection, A/Cross for confirm, B/Circle for back).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Gamepad left stick provides smooth, proportional analog steering.
- [ ] RT (Right Trigger) provides progressive analog throttle [0.0 to 1.0].
- [ ] LT (Left Trigger) provides progressive analog braking and reverse.
- [ ] Face buttons (A/Cross for throttle, B/Circle for handbrake, X/Square for brake) supported as alternative digital layout.
- [ ] Controller hot-plugging works dynamically during menus and gameplay.
- [ ] Menu navigation fully functional via Gamepad D-pad/stick and buttons.

title: Implement comprehensive physics and control test suite (stability, gamepad emulation, benchmarks)
description:
## What
Create a comprehensive test suite verifying digital input smoothing, stability control systems, high-speed cornering stability without spinouts, gamepad analog mapping, and determinism.

## Why
Vehicle dynamics and input algorithms are sensitive to edge cases. Automated tests guarantee that keyboard driving remains stable, assists do not break intentional drifts, and physics stay 100% deterministic across all configurations.

## Reasoning
Writing unit and integration tests for step responses, yaw damping, split-second steering reversals, and high-speed slalom courses validates that the "loss of control on small turns" bug is completely solved and prevents future regressions.

## Considerations
- Test both raw and assisted control modes.
- Verify determinism and replay playback when assists are active.
- Test extreme inputs (full opposite lock at 200 km/h, rapid keyboard tapping, zero-deadzone stick).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Automated tests verify keyboard steering smooth rise/return times and speed attenuation.
- [ ] Slalom and cornering tests prove cars maintain control without unprovoked spinouts on keyboard input.
- [ ] Unit tests for TCS torque modulation and ESC yaw damping under varied surfaces.
- [ ] Gamepad analog normalization and deadzone clamping tests.
- [ ] Full regression suite passes determinism and replay tests.

title: Track Editor: Multi-Shape Surface Zones and Front/Back Layer Ordering
description:
## What
Allow different geometric shapes for surface hazard/runoff zones in the Track Editor (Square [S], Circle [C], Triangle [T], Polygon [P] with arbitrary vertices), and allow configuring their vertical layering relative to the drivable track ribbon (Front / Above Track [F] vs Back / Below Track [B]).

## Why
Currently, surface zones in the editor only support basic AABB boxes and circles with hardcoded layer behavior (only water/oil/ice render on top of the track, while sand/dirt/asphalt always render underneath). Track designers need flexible geometry (triangles for apex curbs/runoffs, polygons for complex landscapes) and explicit front/back layer control (e.g. spilling gravel/sand across the track as a hazard, placing asphalt runoffs underneath the road, or custom water crossing zones).

## Reasoning
- Adding an explicit `layer: SurfaceLayer` (`BelowTrack` vs `AboveTrack`) with serde defaults preserves backward compatibility while granting full layering control to track designers.
- `sample_surface` in physics dynamically resolves surface properties based on layer order: `AboveTrack` zones override track asphalt/dirt, while `BelowTrack` zones only affect vehicles running off the track ribbon.
- Providing single-key shortcuts (`S`, `C`, `T`, `P`, `F`, `B`) in both the tool creation mode and inspector panel enables rapid, ergonomic track authoring.

## Considerations
- Key shortcut disambiguation: `F` (Focus Camera) and `P` (Test Drive) must be context-sensitive (when editing/selecting surface zones, `F` sets Front and `P` sets Polygon).
- Serde backwards-compatibility: Existing tracks saved without an explicit `layer` field must default cleanly to `BelowTrack` (or legacy hazard detection).
- Rendering performance: Triangle and Polygon surface rendering must use efficient fan triangulation / polygon batching in Macroquad.

## Assumptions
- Triangle can be represented geometrically as a 3-vertex Polygon or dedicated helper in the `SurfaceShape` geometry system.
- Front/Back layering applies to both visual rendering order and physics surface query precedence.

## Out of scope
- 3D mesh deformation or arbitrary z-axis heightmaps for surface zones (2.5D layer ordering is sufficient for top-down racing).
- Dynamic runtime fluid simulation for surface zones.
close_reason: Completed: Successfully implemented multi-shape surface zones (Square, Circle, Triangle, Polygon), Front/Back layer ordering (visual rendering + physics precedence), UI selectors/inspector controls/shortcuts (Ctrl+F, Ctrl+B, Ctrl+C, Ctrl+T, Ctrl+P), and multi-segment waypoint selection and batch editing.

title: Core Data Model & Surface Layer Physics Precedence
description:
## What
Add `SurfaceLayer` enum and update `SurfaceZone` and `Track::sample_surface` in `crates/tdrace-core` to support explicit front/back layer ordering for all surface types, with full serialization backwards compatibility and physics query precedence.

## Why
Currently, surface zones do not have an explicit layer field; `sample_surface` hardcodes surface types (`Water`, `Oil`, `Ice`) as on-track hazards and others as off-track ground. Explicit layering allows any surface type (sand, grass, dirt, asphalt, water, oil, etc.) to be placed either above or below the track ribbon.

## Reasoning
- Adding `#[serde(default)] pub layer: SurfaceLayer` ensures existing track files load seamlessly without schema breakage.
- `sample_surface` queries `AboveTrack` zones before spline projection, allowing hazards or surface overlays on top of asphalt, and `BelowTrack` zones after spline projection, keeping runoffs under the road.

## Considerations
- Ensure `SurfaceShape::Polygon` point-in-polygon and centroid calculation handle 3-vertex triangles cleanly.
- Verify JSON roundtrip test for old and new track files.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `SurfaceLayer` enum (`BelowTrack`, `AboveTrack`) added to `tdrace-core::track::geometry`.
2. `SurfaceZone` includes `#[serde(default)] pub layer: SurfaceLayer` field with backwards-compatible defaults.
3. `SurfaceShape` supports Polygon/Triangle geometry and containment tests.
4. `Track::sample_surface` samples `AboveTrack` zones first, then track ribbon/curbs, then `BelowTrack` zones, then default terrain.
5. All unit tests in `tdrace-core` for surface sampling, containment, and serialization pass.
close_reason: Completed: Added SurfaceLayer (BelowTrack, AboveTrack) with backwards-compatible serde default, updated Track::sample_surface hierarchy, added SurfaceShape helper methods, and verified with unit tests.

title: Multi-Layer & Multi-Shape Track Rendering Pipeline
description:
## What
Update the track rendering pipeline in `crates/tdrace-app/src/render/track.rs` and `crates/tdrace-app/src/ui/track_preview.rs` to render surface zones in two distinct passes (`BelowTrack` under the road, `AboveTrack` on top of the road) and support all geometric shapes (Square, Circle, Triangle, Polygon).

## Why
Visual rendering must match physical surface collision: off-track runoffs should sit beneath the asphalt and curbs, while on-track hazards (or designer-placed top layers) should render directly over the drivable ribbon. Furthermore, triangles and arbitrary polygons must render with proper filled triangulation and clean borders.

## Reasoning
- Macroquad `draw_triangle` and fan triangulation allow efficient rendering of arbitrary convex and simple polygons without heavy external triangulation libraries.
- Two-pass ground rendering (`render_surface_zones_pass(track, SurfaceLayer::BelowTrack)` and `render_surface_zones_pass(track, SurfaceLayer::AboveTrack)`) keeps the pipeline clean and deterministic.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `render_ground_track` renders `BelowTrack` surface zones before track ribbon/curbs and `AboveTrack` surface zones after track ribbon/curbs.
2. All `SurfaceShape` variants (Square/AABB, Circle, OrientedBox, Triangle, Polygon) render filled shapes and perimeter outlines correctly in `render_surface_shape`.
3. Track preview in `ui/track_preview.rs` renders layered surface zones and polygon/triangle shapes accurately.
4. Render tests and visual benchmarks pass cleanly.
close_reason: Completed: Implemented two-pass ground track rendering (BelowTrack under road, AboveTrack over road) and full support for all shapes (Square, Circle, Triangle, Polygon) in main renderer and track previews.

title: Editor Tool Placement & Interactions for Multi-Shapes (Square, Circle, Triangle, Polygon)
description:
## What
Implement creation, dragging, duplication, deletion, and real-time gizmo previews for Square, Circle, Triangle, and Polygon surface zones in `crates/tdrace-app/src/editor/tools.rs`.

## Why
Track creators need intuitive, responsive editing tools for creating various hazard/surface shapes. Polygons and triangles allow custom track borders and corner runoffs that cannot be represented by simple bounding boxes.

## Reasoning
- Reusing the `active_polygon_vertices` buffer (similar to polygon obstacles) ensures consistent UX across polygon obstacles and surface zones.
- Interactive closing detection (< 1.5m from start vertex) or keypress finalization makes multi-vertex polygon drawing natural and error-free.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `SurfaceShapeType` enum expanded to support `Square`, `Circle`, `Triangle`, and `Polygon`.
2. Interactive creation workflows implemented:
   - Square: drag rectangle bounding box.
   - Circle: drag center + radius.
   - Triangle: 3-click vertex placement or drag bounding triangle.
   - Polygon: multi-click arbitrary vertices with start-vertex closing snap or Enter key.
3. Gizmo previews render real-time drag outlines, vertex dots, and polygon construction lines.
4. Position dragging, translation, duplication (`Ctrl+D`), and deletion (`Del`) work seamlessly for all 4 shapes.
5. Unit tests for tool placement and vertex handling pass.
close_reason: Completed: Expanded SurfaceShapeType to Square, Circle, Triangle, Polygon; implemented multi-shape placement workflows, gizmo construction previews, and layer helpers.

title: End-to-End Integration Tests & Presets Validation
description:
## What
Implement automated end-to-end and regression tests for multi-shape surface zones and front/back layering across `tdrace-core` and `tdrace-app`, and verify that all presets and editor tools work flawlessly.

## Why
Ensures that the new multi-shape geometry, front/back layer rendering, physics sampling precedence, and editor UX are rock solid, backwards compatible, and regression-free.

## Reasoning
- Integration tests simulating the exact editor workflow (tool activation, shape selection, placement, layer toggling with F/B, undo/redo, file save/load, car surface queries) guarantee end-to-end correctness.

title: Track Editor: Multi-Segment Selection and Batch Property Editing
description:
## What
Allow track creators to select multiple track waypoints/segments simultaneously (via Shift+Click, Ctrl/Cmd+Click, marquee box drag, or Ctrl+A) and apply batch edits to all selected segments at once (adjusting track width, surface type, curb toggles, elevation, moving together, duplicating, or deleting).

## Why
Currently, modifying a section of a track (e.g. widening a 10-waypoint straight, applying dirt surface to a rally sector, toggling curbs along an entire chicane, or elevating a multi-point bridge overpass) requires tedious node-by-node editing. Multi-segment selection with batch property application dramatically accelerates track design workflows.

## Reasoning
- Extending `Selection` to support multiple selected waypoint indices (e.g. `Selection::MultipleWaypoints(HashSet<usize>)` or dedicated multi-selection state in `EditorState`) allows flexible composite interactions without breaking single-selection mechanics.
- Inspector UI detects multi-selection and displays batch property controls that apply mutations across all selected waypoints in a single atomic undo/redo transaction (`state.record_undo()`).
- Drag translation applies the mouse delta vector uniformly to all selected points, preserving curve geometry.

## Considerations
- When deleting multiple non-contiguous waypoints, ensure spline rebuild maintains a valid closed loop (minimum 3 waypoints required).
- Shift+Click range selection: selecting waypoint A then Shift+Clicking waypoint B should select the contiguous path between A and B along the spline.

## Out of scope
- Multi-selection across different entity types simultaneously (e.g. selecting a waypoint and an obstacle together).
acceptance_criteria:
1. Multi-selection support for track waypoints and segments via Shift+Click, Ctrl/Cmd+Click, Drag Box / Marquee select, and Ctrl+A (Select All).
2. Visual gizmo highlights for all selected waypoints and intermediate track ribbons.
3. Batch Inspector controls:
   - Batch track width adjustment slider/buttons.
   - Batch surface type application (Asphalt, Dirt, Curb).
   - Batch left/right curb toggles.
   - Batch elevation adjustment for overpasses and bridges.
4. Batch translation: dragging any selected node moves all selected segments proportionally.
5. Batch operations: Delete [Del], Duplicate [Ctrl+D], and Clear Selection [Esc].
6. Undo/Redo integration records single atomic snapshot for batch actions.
7. Unit and integration tests for multi-segment selection and batch editing pass.
close_reason: Completed: Implemented multi-segment waypoint selection (Shift/Ctrl toggle, group dragging, group duplication, group deletion) and batch inspector editing (width, curbs, surface, elevation).

title: Configurable Track Off-Track Surface Property & Pallid Backdrop Rendering
description:
## What
Add full support for configuring the global off-track surface type as a per-track property (default_surface with options: Grass, Sand, Dirt, Asphalt) selectable in the track editor, and dynamically render the game/editor/preview backdrops with a matching, slightly pallid/lighter palette shade.

## Background
Circuits do not have hardcoded stage classifications like 'desert rally stages' beyond their module assignments. Instead, each track should define its own off-track terrain property (default_surface), choosing among Grass, Sand, Dirt, or Asphalt. When off-track, the game world backdrop and physics should match this chosen surface, with background colors visually resembling the track editor surface zones but tinted slightly lighter/more pallid.

## Scope & Deliverables
1. Core & Palette: Add pallid backdrop colors for Grass, Sand, Dirt, and Asphalt; ensure Track.default_surface cleanly supports all 4 options.
2. Track Editor: Add interactive UI controls in the track editor properties panel to inspect and change track.default_surface.
3. Rendering: Replace hardcoded grass clear background with dynamic backdrop rendering based on the active track's default_surface in the game session, editor viewport, and track preview thumbnails.
4. Testing: Add automated tests for default surface mutation, serialization round-trips, and background color lookups.

## Assumptions
- Supported off-track options for track default_surface are Grass, Sand, Dirt, and Asphalt.
- Placed surface zones (surface_zones) continue to render with their existing saturated colors, while the global off-track backdrop uses lighter/pallid variants.
close_reason: Completed

title: Define pallid backdrop palette colors & core track default surface helpers
description:
## What
Add backdrop palette color constants and lookup helpers for off-track terrain surfaces (Grass, Sand, Dirt, Asphalt) with slightly lighter/pallid tones compared to placed surface zones.

## Why
Currently main.rs hardcodes Palette::GRASS as the clear color. We need a unified lookup function get_track_backdrop_color(surface: SurfaceType) -> Color that returns a softer, lighter/pallid backdrop shade corresponding to each supported off-track surface type.

## Considerations
- Grass: Lighter/pallid turf green (softer than Palette::GRASS)
- Dirt: Lighter/pallid earth brown (softer than Palette::DIRT)
- Sand: Lighter/pallid warm sand/beige (softer than Palette::SAND)
- Asphalt: Lighter/pallid cool road grey (softer than Palette::ASPHALT)
acceptance_criteria:
- Palette defines dedicated backdrop colors for Grass, Sand, Dirt, and Asphalt.
- Helper function maps SurfaceType to its corresponding pallid backdrop Color.
- Default surface types supported for global off-track are Grass, Sand, Dirt, and Asphalt.
close_reason: Completed

## Considerations

- Undo/redo and track saving must preserve the updated default_surface.
